text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on continuous-batching path (us-west2). Paging oncall. Affected route: /v1/generate (streaming). Autoscaler triggered paging. Metrics: p95 ~ 340ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 1.1s -> 6.5s. Paging count: 23 across pool-contbatch-01.

maya: oncall here. seeing tail spikes on cont-batch nodes, streaming stalls reported. Is this correlated with a large influx of long sequences?

sam: quick check — yes, traffic shift from chat-bot partner at 10:02 caused a batch mix to include many 2048-token requests. Queueing shows mixed-seqlen amplification. Logs: `batcher: forming batch size=32 seqlens=[16,18,20,2048,...]`

jordan: those 2k requests are padding-amplifiers. cont-batch packer holding short requests behind long one — causing streaming preempt stall. Paging due to KV cache thrash too (eviction spikes).

li: are we hitting KV eviction on the GPUs? I see KV miss rate jump at 10:03 and paging counters on the driver. Kernel logs attached: ```WARN kv_cache: evicting entry, size=14MB ts=10:03:14```

maya: immediate actions: 1) split heavy customers to non-contbatch pool (route to streaming-only fallback), 2) temp reduce max_batch_size, 3) bump preempt threshold to prefer shorter sequences.

sam: initiating routing rule: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.local/routing -d '{"selector":"partner-x","route":"stream-only-usw2"}'` -> applied. verifying... traffic shift observed.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started job rollback-traffic-routing job/route-split-4923. Job succeeded in 12s.

jordan: while routing helps, cont-batch packer still has inflight long seqs — suggest: set `max_batch_size` from 64 -> 24 on pool-contbatch-01 to reduce wait time. Also enable mixed-seqlen-shed for sequences >1024.

li: running quick config change on pool-contbatch-01: ```rdctl pool update pool-contbatch-01 --max-batch-size=24 --shed-threshold=1024``` Applying now.

incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: pool-contbatch-01 updated by li at 10:06:12.

maya: monitoring p95/p99. Sam, can you run a canary to ensure short sequences still get low latency?

sam: canary started: `wrk -c50 -d30s -t4 https://usw2.redwood.local/v1/generate -H 'x-client:canary' -p small-prompts.json` Will paste results.

support-bot: NOTE: Customer partner-x experiencing degraded streaming for ~3 mins. Support ticket #8521 created and linked. No external customer notifications yet — waiting for impact assessment.

jordan: observing KV eviction rate falling, queue length reducing. p95 back to ~420ms, p99 trending down toward ~850ms. Streaming stalls count decreased by 70%.

li: canary results: p50 120ms p95 380ms p99 760ms under new config. Looks healthy.

maya: good. next steps: 1) keep routing split for 30m, 2) schedule policy change to make `shed-threshold=1024` permanent after postmortem, 3) follow up with partner engineering to patch client to avoid 2k burst.

sam: creating short-lived dashboard link for SRE + product: https://grafana.redwood/d/contbatch/incident-4923456789 (pinning p95/p99, paging count, kv-eviction, queue_len).

jordan: note for postmortem: root cause = mixed sequence length amplification + insufficient preemptive shedding + KV cache thrash under long sequences. Mitigations worked: routing fallback, batch size reduction, shedding threshold.

support-bot: update ticket #8521: partner-x impacted for ~5 minutes. Preliminary classification: degraded quality, no data loss. Assigned to cs-rep @olivia.

maya: handing off to night oncall (li) in 20m. li, you're primary — keep routing split until morning and run a 1-hour watch for paging relapse.

li: acknowledged. will keep 30m routing split and 1h watch. If paging > 5 events in 10m, revert to emergency fallback to dedicated nodes.

ops-bot: reminder: incident created INC-2026-4923, severity S2.

sam: notes I'm adding to incident ticket: commands used, config diffs, canary output, dashboards. Will attach logs `contbatch-batcher.log` and kv stats.

jordan: quick config diff snippet for postmortem: ```- max_batch_size: 64+``````+ max_batch_size: 24
- shed_threshold: 2048
+ shed_threshold: 1024
```

maya: thanks team. If any customer escalates, loop in product and legal. I'll update execs with a one-paragraph summary.

li: final check at 10:12:30 - p99 steady at ~620ms, paging events = 2 in last 10m. Marking mitigation stable.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Please file postmortem within 72 hours.

maya: closing handoff thread to li. Oncall off for me.

li: taking over.

sam: thumbs up :thumbsup: — great triage.

jordan: adding action item: automated shed policy by traffic profile (short-heavy vs long-heavy) - assigned to eng-runtime team.

support-bot: ticket #8521 updated: customer notified with timeline and mitigation steps.

maya: end."
